title: वक्रोक्तिका प्रकार र नेपाली लोककविता Bakroktika Prakar a Nepali Lokkabita
nepali: वक्रोक्ति सिद्धान्त पूर्वीय साहित्यको एक प्रसिद्ध सिद्धान्त हो । काव्यमा वक्रोक्तिको आवश्यकता रहेको धारणा भरतमुनिदेखिका सबै मनीषीले राखेको देखिए पनि वक्रोक्तिलाई काव्यविश्लेषणको सैद्धान्तिक आधार दिने चिन्तक दसौँ शताब्दीको उत्तरार्धका कुन्तक हुन् । कुन्तकका अनुसार वक्रोक्ति भनेको विशिष्ट प्रकारको कथन हो र विशिष्ट कथन भनेको कविको विदग्धतापूर्ण अर्थात् चतुरतापूर्वकको कथन हो । यस प्रकारको विशेष कथनबाट सहृदयीहरूको हृदय आह्लादित हुने भएकाले वक्रोक्तिलाई काव्यको आत्मा मानिन्छ । विशेष प्रकारको कथनका लागि वर्ण, पद, वाक्य, प्रकरण तथा समग्र प्रबन्धमा विदग्धतापूर्ण कथनको आवश्यकता पर्दछ । यीमध्ये कुनैमा त्रुटि वा दोष देखिएमा त्यसले समग्र काव्यको आह्लादकत्वमा क्षति पु¥याउँछ । त्यसैले काव्य सर्वाङ्ग विदग्धतापूर्ण कथनमा आबद्ध हुनुपर्दछ । साहित्यमा यसलाई पूर्णपालना गर्ने प्रयास गरिएको पनि हुन्छ । तर लोकसाहित्यसर्वसाधारण जनताको स्वतःस्फूर्त रूपमा प्रस्तुत हुने मौखिक अभिव्यक्ति भएकाले सिद्धान्तको अनुसरणलाई खासै महङ्खव दिइँदैन । त्यसैले लोकसाहित्यको एक भेद मानिने लोककवितामा पनिसिद्धान्तअनुरूपको कथन आवश्यक मानिदैन । तापनि यिनमा लोककविको सहज प्रतिभाको उच्छलन पनि यत्रतत्र छचल्किएकै पाइएको छ । समाजमा प्रचलित लोककविताको विदग्धतापूर्ण कथनका सन्दर्भबाट अध्ययन गर्दै जाँदा कतिपय लोककवितामा वक्रोक्ति सिद्धान्तले मानेका वर्ण, पद, वाक्य आदि भेद र यिनका भेदोपभेदको उपस्थिति रहेको देखिन्छ । लोककवितामा भाव अनुकूलको वर्णको प्रयोग, धातु वा प्रातिपदिकको अर्थपूर्ण प्रयोग, सामान्य भन्दा अलौकिक वा चमत्कारजनक वाक्यको प्रयोग लगायत वक्रोक्ति सिद्धान्तले मानेका विदग्धतापूर्ण अर्थात् चतुरतापूर्वकको कथन भएको देखिन्छ । यस आधारमा लोककविताका प्रयोक्ता सर्वसाधारण भए पनि उनीहरूको सहज प्रतिभाले लोककवितालाई विशिष्टता प्रदान गरेका छन् र यिनले सहृदयीहरूको हृदयलाई आनन्दातिरेक तुल्याएका छन् भन्ने निष्कर्ष यस लेखमा निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The Vakrokti theory is a renowned doctrine in Eastern literature. Although all thinkers from Bharata Muni onward are seen to have held the view that Vakrokti is necessary in poetry, the thinker who gave Vakrokti a theoretical foundation for poetic analysis was Kuntaka in the latter half of the tenth century. According to Kuntaka, Vakrokti is a specialized form of expression, and specialized expression is the poet's witty, that is, ingenious statement. Because this special form of statement gladdens the hearts of discerning connoisseurs, Vakrokti is regarded as the soul of poetry. For a specialized kind of statement, witty expression is required across phonemes, words, sentences, episodes, and the overall composition. If an error or flaw is seen in any of these, it damages the delightfulness of the overall poetry. Therefore, poetry must be entirely bound in witty expression. In literature, attempts have also been made to comply with this fully. However, because folk literature is the spontaneous oral expression of common people, adherence to doctrine is not given much importance. For that reason, in folk poetry, which is regarded as a variety of folk literature, expression conforming to theory is not considered necessary either. Even so, the spontaneous overflow of the folk poet's innate genius is found splashing everywhere within them. When studying folk poetry prevalent in society from the standpoint of witty expression, the presence of phonemic, lexical, sentential, and other categories acknowledged by the Vakrokti theory, along with their subcategories, is seen in several folk poems. In folk poetry, the use of phonemes suited to sentiment, meaningful use of roots or nominal bases, use of extraordinary or wondrous sentences beyond the ordinary, and other witty, that is, clever expressions acknowledged by the Vakrokti theory are seen to exist. On this basis, this article draws the conclusion that even though the creators of folk poetry are ordinary people, their natural talent has bestowed distinctiveness upon folk poetry and brought profound joy to the hearts of discerning lovers of poetry.
british_english: The Vakrokti doctrine is a celebrated theory in Eastern literature. Although all thinkers from Bharata Muni onwards appear to have maintained that Vakrokti is indispensable to poetry, the thinker who provided Vakrokti with a theoretical foundation for poetic analysis was Kuntaka in the latter half of the tenth century. According to Kuntaka, Vakrokti signifies a distinctive mode of expression, and distinctive expression denotes the poet's ingenious, or witty, utterance. Because this manner of special utterance delights the hearts of sensitive readers, Vakrokti is considered the soul of poetry. For a distinctive mode of utterance, ingenious expression is required across letter, word, sentence, episode and the work as a whole. Should an error or fault appear in any of these, it impairs the capacity of the entire poem to give delight. Poetry must therefore be framed entirely in ingenious utterance. In literature, endeavours have indeed been made to observe this fully. However, since folk literature is the spontaneous oral expression of ordinary people, adherence to theory is scarcely accorded importance. Consequently, in folk poetry, which is regarded as a branch of folk literature, expression adhering to doctrine is not deemed necessary either. Even so, the outburst of the folk poet's spontaneous gift is found overflowing here and there within them. As one studies the folk poetry current in society from the perspective of witty utterance, the presence of distinctions of phoneme, word and sentence recognised by the Vakrokti doctrine, together with their sub-distinctions, is seen to exist in various folk poems. In folk poetry, the employment of phonemes suited to emotion, the meaningful employment of verbal roots or nominal stems, the use of extraordinary or miraculous sentences surpassing the commonplace, and other ingenious, that is, artful utterances recognised by the Vakrokti doctrine are seen to occur. On this basis, the conclusion drawn in this article is that although the practitioners of folk poetry are ordinary people, their natural talent has conferred distinction upon folk poetry and filled the hearts of discerning appreciators with an ecstasy of joy.
australian_english: The Vakrokti theory is a famous doctrine in Eastern literature. While every scholar from Bharata Muni onwards seems to have held that Vakrokti is needed in poetry, the thinker who gave Vakrokti a theoretical grounding for analysing poetry was Kuntaka in the second half of the tenth century. According to Kuntaka, Vakrokti means a specialised form of expression, and specialised expression means the poet's witty, or clever, statement. Because this special sort of statement brings delight to the hearts of sensitive readers, Vakrokti is treated as the soul of poetry. For a specialised expression, witty expression is needed right across letters, words, sentences, episodes and the work as a whole. If a mistake or fault shows up in any of these, it damages the joy that the poem as a whole can bring. That is why poetry has to be tied up completely in witty expression. In written literature, efforts have certainly been made to stick to this entirely. But because folk literature is the spontaneous spoken expression of everyday people, sticking to theory is not really given much weight. So in folk poetry, which is seen as one branch of folk literature, expression that follows theory is not considered necessary either. Even so, flashes of the folk poet's natural talent are found spilling over here and there throughout them. Looking at the folk poetry circulating in society from the angle of witty expression, the presence of categories recognised by the Vakrokti theory—like letters, words and sentences, along with their subdivisions—can be seen in quite a few folk poems. In folk poetry, using letters to suit the mood, making meaningful use of roots or nominal bases, and using wondrous sentences that go beyond the ordinary show the kind of witty, or clever, expression recognised by the Vakrokti theory. On this basis, this paper concludes that even though everyday folk are the ones making folk poetry, their natural flair gives folk poetry real distinction and brings sheer delight to the hearts of poetry lovers.
informal_english: Vakrokti theory is a right famous doctrine in Eastern literature, so it is. Though every thinker from Bharata Muni onwards reckoned that poetry needs Vakrokti, it was Kuntaka in the latter half o' the tenth century who gave Vakrokti a proper theoretical footing for pulling poetry apart. According to Kuntaka, Vakrokti just means a distinctive kind o' expression, and that distinctive expression is the poet's cannie, witty way with words. Because that special sort o' speaking warms the hearts o' sensitive folk, Vakrokti is taken to be the very soul o' poetry. To pull off that special kind o' speaking, ye need witty expression in the letters, words, sentences, episodes, and the hail composition together. If a flaw or a blunder crops up in any o' them, it spoils the joy o' the entire poem. That's why poetry has got to be bound up top to bottom in clever, cannie speech. Folk have tried hard enough in proper literature to follow this to the letter. But folk literature is just the spontaneous spoken words o' ordinary folk, so nobody gives two hoots about sticking to textbook theory. That's why in folk poetry, which is just a branch o' folk literature, speaking according to the rules isnae thought necessary at all. Mind you, the sudden rush o' the folk poet's natural gift is still seen splashing out all over the place. When ye look at the folk poetry going round the community from the angle o' witty speech, ye can see categories like letters, words, and sentences laid out in Vakrokti theory, along wi' their wee sub-varieties, showing up in a fair few folk poems. In folk poetry, picking sounds to fit the feeling, using roots or word-bases meaningfully, and coming out with wondrous, out-o'-the-ordinary sentences shows the kind o' witty, clever expression that Vakrokti theory talks about. On that basis, this paper concludes that even if the folk making these poems are just ordinary folk, their natural talent gives folk poetry something truly special, bringing pure joy to the hearts o' poetry lovers.
